exposure: Laparotomy-assisted fetoscopic in-utero spina bifida (SB) repair
Traditional open-hysterotomy methods for SB repair
MOMs trial methods for SB repair
cohort: The study included fetuses undergoing laparotomy-assisted fetoscopic in-utero spina bifida repair from Mexico and Colombia, compared against cases from the MOMs trial and other Latin American centers using traditional open-hysterotomy methods.
finding: Laparotomy-assisted fetoscopic spina bifida repair significantly reduced rates of prematurity and cesarean deliveries compared to traditional hysterotomy-based techniques in Latin America, while showing similar hydrocephalus treatment requirements at 12 months.
mod_finding: The laparotomy-assisted fetoscopic repair group exhibited a significantly lower cesarean delivery rate (65.8%) and facilitated vaginal births compared to traditional open-hysterotomy methods.
gest_age: Gestational age at surgery (26+-1.27 weeks for fetoscopic group) and gestational age at delivery (35.3+-3.79 weeks for fetoscopic group, 34.1+-3.1 weeks for MOMs, 34+-3.002 weeks for open-repair)
